analysis.evidence: חֲמֵשׁ supplies the five in חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה, “fifteen cubits,” a measure of how high the waters rose.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, in the form used before עֶשְׂרֵה.

analysis.evidence: In חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה, “fifteen cubits,” עֶשְׂרֵה supplies ten and חֲמֵשׁ supplies five. The feminine form agrees with אַמָּה, “cubit.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, second element of a compound numeral.
analysis.sense: ten, in the numbers eleven to nineteen

analysis.evidence: חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה means “fifteen cubits” and measures how far the floodwaters rose above the mountains.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun used after the numeral חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה.

analysis.evidence: חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה gives the vertical distance, fifteen cubits. מִלְמַעְלָה places the waters that far above the mountains, which the closing clause says were covered.
analysis.morphology: Adverb with prefixed מִן (מִ־ before לְ־) and לְ־, and directional suffix ־ָה.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb גָּבְרוּ agrees with הַמָּיִם, “the waters.” The phrase חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה מִלְמַעְלָה measures their rise at fifteen cubits, and the following clause says the mountains were covered.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with verbal ending ־וּ and no prefix or pronominal suffix.

draft.change: Add a note to the existing Genesis 7:18–20 citation explaining how verse 20 illustrates the body-of-water sense.
draft.definition: מַיִם can denote a body of water, here the floodwaters that covered the mountains.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:20 measures the rise of הַמָּיִם at fifteen cubits and describes the mountains as covered.

analysis.evidence: הַמָּיִם is the subject of the plural verb גָּבְרוּ. The verse measures the waters’ rise in cubits and says that the mountains were covered.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הַ־, which doubles the initial מ.
analysis.sense: a body or flow of water

analysis.evidence: The passive verb וַיְכֻסּוּ agrees with its following subject הֶהָרִים, “the mountains.” The preceding clause names הַמָּיִם, “the waters,” as what rose and covered them.
analysis.morphology: Pual wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ and no suffix pronoun

analysis.evidence: In וַיְכֻסּוּ הֶהָרִים, “the mountains were covered,” הֶהָרִים is the subject of the plural passive verb. The rising floodwaters cover the mountains.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute noun with the prefixed definite article הֶ־.
